name: Articles
moduleIntroduction: Hello! This module is about Articles. Articles are the small words 'a', 'an', 'the', or sometimes no article at all (which we call the "zero article"). These words seem small, but they change the meaning of a noun. Why is this difficult? Because French uses articles all the time, but English sometimes leaves them out.
contrastiveExplanation:
A / AN: Use for one, non-specific thing. Watch out for professions ('He is a teacher', not 'He is teacher').

THE: Use for specific things ('The book on the table').

ZERO ARTICLE (Ø): Use for general plurals and abstract nouns. (French: 'J'aime les chiens' -> English: 'I like dogs', NOT 'the dogs').

commonErrors.frenchConnection: French does not use an article for professions after 'être'.
Information is countable in French (une information).
French uses article for institutions (à l'école).
